title: Infinite-Level Hierarchy of Solvable Quantum Circuits
authors: Michael A. Rampp, Suhail A. Rather, Pieter W. Claeys
abstract: Dual-unitary circuits have emerged as a paradigm of exactly solvable yet non-integrable quantum dynamics. Recently, a generalization of dual unitarity attempting to extend the phenomenology of exactly solvable circuits has been introduced through a hierarchy of conditions, with dual unitarity as the first level. However, beyond the second level the proposed generalized dual-unitary hierarchy ceases to be solvable in the whole spacetime. We present an infinite hierarchy of solvability conditions remedying this problem. These new conditions can be combined with the generalized dual-unitary hierarchy to obtain circuits for which correlation functions and entanglement dynamics can be analyzed exactly in the whole spacetime. We show that this novel hierarchy possesses non-trivial solutions at every level. Our results demonstrate that dual unitarity can be systematically extended while preserving solvability, opening up investigations of exactly solvable non-integrable systems with more general properties.
summary: This paper introduces a comprehensive framework—the Full Dual-Unitary ($	ext{FDU}_k$) hierarchy—to achieve exact solvability for quantum circuits across the entire spacetime. By combining complementary unitarity conditions, the authors overcome previous limitations that restricted solvable regions to finite domains. This opens new avenues for precisely calculating correlation functions and entanglement dynamics in complex, non-integrable quantum systems.
main_problem: The primary goal is to extend the solvability of quantum dynamics beyond the limitations of generalized dual-unitary circuits ($	ext{DU}_k$) to analyze correlation functions and entanglement dynamics across the entire spacetime.
main_result: The authors introduce a novel, infinite hierarchy of conditions ($	ext{FDU}_k$) that remedies the finite spacetime restriction, allowing exact analysis of correlations and entanglement in all regions.
method: The work employs tensor network representations, algebraic constraint derivation from diagram consistency, and analyzing asymptotic behavior via quantum channels to characterize solvability domains.
model_or_system: The system is based on quantum circuits built with dual-unitary gates applied to qubits or qudits in a lattice geometry. The analysis focuses on the structure of these solvable dynamics across spacetime.
key_observables: Correlation functions $C(x, t)$, Entanglement Line Tension ($	ext{ELT}$), and the solvability condition itself (FDU$_k$).
important_parameters: The level of unitarity ($k$), the velocity $v$, and the local Hilbert space dimension ($q$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on constructing complementary dual-unitary conditions ($	ext{DU}^*_k$) to supplement the original hierarchy, and simplifying complex tensor network structures by considering extremal paths.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the logical inclusion of solvability domains ($	ext{FDU}_k = 	ext{DU}^*_k + 	ext{DU}_k$), show the piecewise linear nature of the ELT for $	ext{FDU}_k$ circuits, and depict tensor network diagrams.
paper_structure: The paper systematically introduces the limitations of $	ext{DU}_k$, proposes the complementary conditions ($	ext{DU}^*_k$) to form $	ext{FDU}_k$, derives explicit formulas for correlators in different spacetime path domains (thin/thick), and finally analyzes entanglement scaling via the ELT.
why_interesting: The development of an infinite hierarchy of exactly solvable, non-integrable models provides powerful theoretical tools to study complex quantum many-body dynamics where standard integrability methods fail.
